target_customer: Online shoppers who shop with friends
problem: Online shopping is solitary; shoppers cannot easily consult friends while browsing retailers.
business_model: Free social toolbar overlay on retailer sites; monetization not found (likely affiliate)

founders.name: Tom Saffell
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch Oct 2009 and on YC page

competitors.name: Kaboodle
competitors.what: Social shopping and wish list site owned by Hearst
competitors.traction_then: ranked first in a 2008 social shopping ranking at 68 percent share

competitors.name: ThisNext
competitors.traction_then: listed among top social shopping sites in 2008

competitors.name: Smack Shopping
competitors.what: Earlier social shopping attempt that TechCrunch calls a failure

competitors.name: Fruugo
competitors.what: Earlier social shopping attempt cited by TechCrunch

technical_complexity.rationale: Used a custom proxy server to wrap retailer sites with a chat and buddy panel, plus Facebook Connect, per TechCrunch October 2009; proxying third party stores is fragile.

defensibility.rationale: Overlay and chat were copyable; relied on retailer sites it did not control and no network effect before critical mass.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying it; Kaboodle later launched Kaboodle Together co-browsing per a 2012 article. Plurchase outcome not documented.

market_need_then: Social commerce was a hot theme in 2008 to 2009 with multiple funded sites, but TechCrunch noted earlier attempts had failed, so demand for shopping with friends was unproven.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches for name origin, logo, mascot, rebrands and press about the brand returned nothing about this company, so the brand is rated at the floor on absence of evidence only. The name reads as a blend of plural and purchase, but no source confirms it.

outcome_analysis: Plurchase launched in October 2009 as a social toolbar proxy over Zappos, Amazon and Craigslist. It raised only the YC amount reported by one database and is marked dead there. No post-mortem exists, so the cause is not public; the listed failure factors are inferences from earlier failed social shopping attempts and dependence on retailer sites.
notes: plurchase.com did not resolve in this session (dead or blocked). The $20K round rests on CB Insights only. Failure factors are inferred, not sourced. YC page lists Ferber, Mao and Saffell; team size 2.
